task.text:
Design a stack that supports push, pop in constant time.
Implement the MinStack class:
MinStack() initializes the stack object.
void push (int val) pushes the element val onto the stack.
void pop() removes the element on the top of the stack. Use Java

attempts.high: I want to build a stack data structure in Java that does something clever beyond the basics — push and pop in constant time, sure, but pick an interesting extra capability the structure can support in O(1) and design the whole thing around it. Your call on what that feature is, what the class is named, and how the internals work. Surprise me with the design, then implement it.
attempts.low: Implement the MinStack class in Java exactly as specified. MinStack() initializes the stack object. void push(int val) pushes val onto the stack. void pop() removes the top element. int top() returns the top element. int getMin() retrieves the minimum element in the stack. All operations must run in O(1) time. Use two stacks (one for values, one for tracking the minimum). Follow these method names and signatures precisely, no extra methods.
reasons: leakage on non-target axis 'difficulty': HIGH=4, LOW=2 (differ by 2, max allowed 1). Equalize this dimension across the two versions.
competence check failed: verifier judges the two versions to demand different underlying skills. Keep the required competences identical.
